newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Accor wants Morocco to upgrade tourism.
newsitem.headline: Accor wants Morocco to upgrade tourism.

text.p: French hotel group Accor, which has agreed with the Moroccan government to help set up a $100 million investment fund for tourism, said on Friday the country needs foreign expertise in its tourism industry.

Accor's managing director Gerard Pelisson told a news conference that "...generally speaking, the Moroccan tourism sector has been run for a long time by amateurs...Time has come the sector should be managed by professionals."

Pelisson conferred with government officials including King Hassan on Thursday, after the signature of a convention to set up an international investment fund aimed at upgrading tourism projects and building new ones.
"Morocco has a solid tourism industry which could achieve better results and attract up to 5.0 million visitors annually, excluding North Africans," Pelisson said.
But it "needed foreign investors' help and their know-how," Pelisson said.

Since the 1991 Gulf war the number of foreign visitors has not exceeded 3.0 million a year, officials said. Tourism receipts dropped to 9.9 billion dirhams ($1.15 billion) in 1995, from 11.3 billion dirhams ($1.31 billion) in the previous year, the finance ministry said.

Pelisson said Accord had drawn up a long-term strategy to develop tourism, targetting middle class tourists, in close cooperation with Moroccan business and transport groups including the country's airline Royal Air Maroc.
The group, which expected to play "the locomotive role" to boost Morocco's tourism sector would invest 1.7 billion dirhams in joint ventures, starting from next year, officials said.
It plans to invest in hotels and other leisure facilities in the tourist cities of Marrakesh and Fez.

Pelisson said the group was interested in the continuing programme which is expected to privatise a total of 37 hotels by 1998. Morocco has sold 18 hotels to foreign or local investors since 1993 when the privatisation of 114 firms started.
Earlier this month, the privatisation ministry offered for sale nine hotels at a total minimum price of 95.9 million dirhams.

The hotels are mainly sited in the south including the tourist city of Marrakesh. Two are in Chefchaouen and Oujda, respectively in the north and east, and one in the Atlantic port city of Casablanca.
Accor has a network of 2,400 hotels in 120 countries, including 40 units in Africa. It employs a staff 120,000.
